pages.title: Participation
pages.content:
## SingleTree Project The SingleTree project aims to create a smarter forestry system by focusing on individual trees. This approach will help forests adapt to climate change, become more resilient, and allow for more sustainable use of wood resources. SingleTree will develop advanced methods to monitor forests based on artificial intelligence and remote sensing, adaptive single-tree level management solutions, intelligent machines for implementing single-tree operations, and improved traceability and ability to predict wood quality early in the value chain as a foundation for optimised biomass supply. To read more, visit https://singletree.eu/
# Objective of the benchmark The objective of this benchmark is to gather and evaluate the performance of sensor- and platform-agnostic whorl detection and stem profile algorithms. The result will provide the SingleTree project with methods that can be used further down the project chain. # Prize The top five participants will have the opportunity to co-author an article about this benchmark. Each team can nominate up to two people who will be registered as co-authors. # How to participate ## Read the terms for entering Go to the terms tab under Get Started and read the terms for entering. If you fail to follow these terms, you will be removed from the competition. In your submission, you MUST provide name, affiliation (with contact information) and a short description of the method with a link to a GitHub repository. ## Download the dataset The dataset, **FOR-wood**, is available for download from Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23012506 ## Benchmarking For evaluation the participant should use their model on the downloaded test set to predict either whorl-positions relative to the ground, the stem profile diameter, or both and output two tables (*.csv) containing predictions for all trees in the test data set. For the whorl detection task, submit a `branch_references.csv` table with the following columns and capitalization: `TreeID`, `Z`, `whorl_number` The scorer matches predictions using `TreeID` and `Z`, where `Z` is the whorl height in metres and `whorl_number` identifies the whorl order. |TreeID|Z|whorl_number| |---|---|---| |221|10.8434|1| |221|11.2577|2| |221|11.5477|3| |n|...|...| For the stem profile prediction task, submit a `stem_references.csv` table with the following columns and capitalization: `TreeID`, `Z`, `D` `Z` is the height in metres and `D` is the predicted stem diameter in metres. Provide values at 0.6 m, 1.3 m, 2 m, and then every metre up the length of the tree. If values are not provided exactly at the evaluation heights, the scorer linearly interpolates the submitted profile. |TreeID|Z|D| |---|---|---| |313|0.4903|0.30539| |313|1.1375|0.29004| |313|1.8426|0.27856| |313|4.8407|0.25084| |n|...|...| Make sure that the column names are exactly the same as stated here. The zip archive itself can be named anything, but it may contain either or both CSV files, and each included file must use its exact corresponding filename: ```text your_submission.zip ├── branch_references.csv └── stem_references.csv ``` ## Submission limits You may submit up to 2 times per day (20 total for the phase). The daily limit is set to 2 rather than 1 so that if a submission errors out (e.g. a naming or column mismatch), you still have a same-day chance to fix it and resubmit. ## Viewing your results After submitting, publish your result to the leaderboard from your submissions panel. The leaderboard is sorted by F1 (whorl detection) by default - if you only submitted stem profile predictions, click on a stem profile column header (e.g. RMSE (Stem)) to sort the leaderboard by that metric instead and see where your submission ranks.

pages.title: Dataset
pages.content:
# Dataset
For this benchmark, we have assembled a dataset consisting of indivdual tree point clouds together with annotations describing whorl positions along the stem as well as stem taper. The data has been pooled from Sweden, Finland and Norway and consists mainly of Scott's Pine trees with a smaller proportion Norway Spruce. 

The dataset, **FOR-wood**, is available for download from Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23012506

The data consist of:
* **Training data**: tree point clouds (laz files) with whorl and taper annotations (`branch_references.csv`, `stem_references.csv`)
* **Test data**: only tree point clouds (laz files), no annotations

**License:** [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) (Attribution-ShareAlike). You may share and adapt the dataset, even commercially, as long as you give appropriate credit and license any derivative datasets under the same terms.
